title: Article on Changes to the Contracted Scope — Retrofit Projects
content:
# Article on Changes to the Contracted Scope

Contract article of Equipment Replacement & Retrofit Projects on change orders and the change allowance.

## Clause 1 — Pricing and the allowance

A change to the contracted scope is priced at cost plus the class's change order markup and is issued against the project's change allowance. The allowance is credited at award as the class's portion of the contract value: the contract value multiplied by the class's allowance rate, rounded to the nearest cent. Changes are drawn from the allowance first and the remainder is added to the contract value. The allowance is never refunded if it goes unused, because it is an authority to spend and not a deposit.

## Clause 2 — Authorisation

A change whose value passes the class's authorisation threshold is not issued until the owner's written authorisation for that change order is recorded in the office records; a verbal instruction on site, however senior the person giving it, is never enough for such a change. The record that counts is the authorisation recorded against that change order's own number.

## Clause 3 — No second issue

A change order that already carries an authorisation is not issued a second time for the same change. The project's change order entries, read by change order number and the authorisation each carries, decide it.

## Clause 4 — Response period and schedule impact

A requested change is priced inside the class's response period, counted in business days from the day the owner asked for it. Where a change adds days to the work, those days extend the guaranteed completion date by the schedule impact stated on the change order.

## Running totals on a project

The value of change orders issued on a project is the total of its change order entries issued from the award day onward, and the schedule impact on a project is the total of the impact days stated on its change order entries issued from the mobilisation day onward.

## Worked illustrations (hypothetical)

- Cost of a change USD 4000, class markup 20 per cent: the change order is priced at USD 4800.
- Allowance credited at award on a USD 200000 contract in a class with a 5 per cent allowance rate: USD 10000. A first change order of USD 4800 is drawn wholly from the allowance, leaving USD 5200; a second of USD 9000 draws the remaining 5200 and adds USD 3800 to the contract value.
- A change order of USD 6000 in a class whose threshold is USD 5000 has passed the threshold and is issued only once the owner's written authorisation naming that change order is recorded; a site superintendent's verbal agreement is not an authorisation. A change order of exactly USD 5000 has not passed it.
